priority.override_reason: Rank-one controlflow-recursive is dominated by the already rejected direct-leaf/frame and complete compact-dispatch mechanisms. The current rank-two A* and rank-three hash-map sources both repeatedly construct ordinary same-field receivers, while rank-four raytrace independently profiles the same class-field/object-storage route. This is a distinct representation change, not another direct-leaf or cache-entry variation.

mechanism.summary: Let repeated ordinary user-constructor receivers share immutable property shapes, then transition those shapes on matching ordinary named additions so values stay in compact ordered slots instead of every instance growing an independent small vector or dynamic name map. Extend the existing shape-slot cache route to re-read live data descriptors after ordinary value writes.
mechanism.generality: A receiver is selected only because it was allocated for a user bytecode constructor and its actual own string-property additions establish the same ordered shape as a prior successful construction of that bytecode. A transition depends only on the live parent shape and added key. It does not inspect benchmark names, source paths, function names, inputs, iteration counts, or results. Objects with a different insertion order, deletion, unsupported storage mutation, exotics, proxies, symbols, or a missing shape retain the existing compact or dynamic storage behavior.
semantic_risks: preserving OrdinarySet and DefineProperty descriptor, setter, Proxy, extensibility, and prototype-chain behavior before a shape slot is populated
preserving absence and enumeration order for partially initialized constructors, duplicate writes, deletions, array-index keys, and descriptor replacement
invalidating identity or shape slot caches on every structural change while allowing ordinary value writes to expose the current value and current writable/accessor state
ensuring a constructor that throws, returns another object, uses Reflect.construct, or diverges in field order cannot expose a partially learned layout as an observable property
